questions.scope: Owl species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common names and scientific names count. An owlet-nightjar or a nighthawk is not an owl.
questions.rationale: One recognizable whole animal group, with a complete publisher species inventory and independent familiar-name cases. No country, colour, habitat or other tag creates extra questions.

questions.scope: Parrot species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common and scientific names count. Pet colour mutations share their species identity; a bird is not a parrot just because its name contains that word.
questions.rationale: One recognizable whole animal group, with a complete publisher species inventory and independent familiar-name cases. No country, colour, habitat or other tag creates extra questions.

questions.scope: Species in the eBird/Clements penguin order and established common group names count. English or scientific names count. Puffins and auks are different kinds of bird.
questions.rationale: One recognizable whole animal group, with a complete publisher species inventory and independent familiar-name cases. No country, colour, habitat or other tag creates extra questions.

questions.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named bat groups, count. Common names and documented scientific names count. A flying fox is a bat; a flying squirrel is not. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory.
questions.rationale: One recognizable whole animal group, with a complete publisher species inventory and independent familiar-name cases. No country, colour, habitat or other tag creates extra questions.
